newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks edge up after zigzagging on Dow.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks edge up after zigzagging on Dow.

text.p: Mexican stocks inched up for the fourth session in a row Tuesday in volatile trading due to the swings in the U.S. market and light profit-taking.

"The bourse was volatile due to skittishness on international markets ahead of U.S. inflation data, which makes the market nervous here also," said Esteban Rojas, associate research director at the Arka brokerage.
The leading IPC share index ended up 0.65 point, or 0.02 percent, at 3,930.74.
The Dow Jones industrial average meanwhile closed down 18.54 points at 7,274.21.
Trading volume of 121.2 million shares was much brisker than for many recent sessions due to the presence of foreign investors.
Traders said although the IPC edged ahead, blue chips as a whole were mixed, with decliners outpacing gainers by 20 to 10, and five unchanged.
Telecomms firm Telmex and financial stock Bancomer weighed most on the downside. The two stocks together accounted for one fifth of all shares traded.
"They took profits on Telmex and Bancomer. Telmex ADRs had trouble breaking resistance at 44," a desk trader said.
Telmex L shares ended down 10 centavos (1 cent) at 17.24 pesos ($2.18), while its ADRs closed off 1/4 at 43-1/2 in Wall Street trading.
Holding company Accelsa gained eight centavos (1 cent) to 2.15 pesos (27 cents), while retail chain Cifra also ended up eight centavos (1 cent), at 12.68 pesos ($1.60).
Holding company Grupo Sidek and its tourist arm Situr ended topped the prominent gainers' list.
"Sidek gained on thin volume. They are still speculating over a financial restructuring deal, but there is nothing new," a trader said.
Sidek gained nine centavos (1 cent) to 62 centavos (8 cent s), while Situr closed up six centavos (less than 1 ce nt) at 48 centavos (6 cents).
